title: Reproducible eradication of metastatic carcinoma

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a treatment platform that reliably produces lasting, treatment-free complete remission in most patients across several common metastatic carcinomas: cancers of epithelial tissues that have spread to distant sites. Its intended capability is to eliminate malignant populations throughout the body while preserving essential normal tissue. This is a proposed clinical breakthrough, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The target includes heterogeneous metastatic clones, cells that lose a treatment’s target antigen, and dormant residual cells that could later restart disease. Cellular therapies, immune therapies, drugs or combinations could contribute; the concept does not require CAR-T therapy specifically. Dormant-cell clearance is an intended requirement, although the supplied CAR-T review does not specifically establish how such cells resist treatment or how to eliminate them.

The defining outcome would be reproducible, durable freedom from metastatic carcinoma after treatment ends. Tumor shrinkage, complete remission on available assessments, prolonged survival and biological eradication are related but distinct outcomes. A convincing clinical demonstration could establish sustained remission and a low observed risk of recurrence without proving that every malignant cell has been removed.

significance.text: Metastatic disease accounts for a substantial share of the burden of fatal solid cancer. A Norwegian national registry analysis, published in 2019 and examining deaths in 2015, found that 66.7% of solid-tumor deaths were registered with metastases as a contributing cause. The authors identified underreporting of metachronous metastases—those discovered after the initial diagnosis—but could not determine the precise proportion of deaths caused by metastases. The result supports the importance of metastatic disease; it does not establish a universal causal fraction for other countries, periods or tumor populations.

Conditional impact assessment: a safe platform that produced lasting complete remission in most patients across several common metastatic carcinomas would create a broadly reproducible, potentially curative capability for established metastatic disease. Its direct importance would come from sustained freedom from recurrence and reduced mortality across multiple cancer types, rather than a short extension of median time before progression. Acceptable toxicity is integral to that advance: eliminating cancer at the cost of disabling or fatal normal-tissue injury would not fulfill the concept.

Conditional downstream possibilities include fewer repeated treatment courses, less cumulative treatment burden and more years lived without active cancer therapy. These benefits would depend on actual durability, adverse effects, manufacturing requirements, cost and delivery capacity. Demonstrated success in several carcinomas would establish meaningful breadth, but would not establish efficacy in every carcinoma or make treatment universally accessible.

As an illustrative analogy, the ambition is a shift toward reliably curative treatment comparable in scale to the historical treatment successes invoked for selected leukemias and germ-cell tumors. The supplied sources do not document that treatment history or justify a quantitative comparison. The significance of this concept therefore rests on its proposed clinical outcomes, independently of that analogy.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved target is coordinated clearance of diverse metastatic populations with a sufficient margin of safety for normal tissues. The supplied October 2025 CAR-T review documents several obstacles: few truly tumor-specific target antigens, variable antigen expression within tumors, antigen escape, dense stromal barriers, an immunosuppressive tumor environment and off-tumor toxicity. These provide a concrete engineering basis for the challenge, while remaining evidence about CAR-T approaches rather than proof of the limitations of every treatment modality.

The comparison with CD19-directed treatment explains an important safety distinction. Depletion of normal B cells after CD19 targeting can be clinically managed. Many candidate solid-tumor antigens are also expressed on essential normal tissues, where comparable destruction may be unacceptable. Transferring success therefore requires more selective recognition, safer control of treatment activity or another way to separate malignant cells from indispensable healthy cells; target recognition alone is insufficient.

Treatment must also reach malignant cells through stromal and physical barriers and remain effective despite suppressive immune cells and metabolic stress. Antigen diversity creates an additional escape route: eliminating one target-positive population can leave another population able to persist. The review presents multi-antigen approaches as promising research that still requires refinement to deliver durable, consistent benefit, rather than as an established solution.

Proposed additional requirement: the platform should prevent relapse from dormant or otherwise undetected residual disease. This creates both a treatment problem and a measurement problem—how to affect clinically hidden cells, and how to distinguish their elimination from prolonged inactivity. The supplied evidence does not resolve either question, so dormant-cell eradication remains part of the intended capability rather than a documented mechanism or demonstrated result.

current_state.text: The review published on 27 October 2025 reports seven FDA-approved CAR-T products for hematologic malignancies, targeting CD19 or B-cell maturation antigen, and no approved CAR-T therapy for solid tumors. These statements describe the review’s dated account. No freshness search record was supplied, so they do not verify regulatory status or the comprehensive treatment landscape as of 1 November 2026.

The review reports that CLDN18.2-targeted satricabtagene autoleucel, or satri-cel, improved median progression-free survival from 1.77 to 3.25 months in a randomized phase 2 trial involving previously treated advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer. It also reports an overall-survival improvement, but the supplied review findings do not provide a numerical estimate for that endpoint. These are reported clinical results, not projections; the primary trial itself was not supplied for separate assessment. The progression-free survival medians demonstrate clinical activity but do not establish lasting eradication, and they cannot determine whether particular patients experienced much longer benefit.

The same review describes individual complete responses, including one lasting more than 30 months in diffuse midline glioma. That example shows why the solid-tumor literature should not be reduced to short gains in median progression-free survival. However, glioma is outside the carcinoma scope, and an individual durable response does not establish reproducible remission in a majority across several common metastatic carcinomas.

The earlier research also invokes checkpoint-inhibitor cures in subsets of melanoma, lung cancer and mismatch-repair-deficient tumors. The supplied source findings do not establish those cure claims or their rates, so they cannot serve here as verified milestones. This evidence gap does not show that such outcomes are false. Melanoma also lies outside carcinoma, while mismatch-repair deficiency identifies a biological subgroup rather than a single carcinoma histology. Evidence about CAR-T approval status alone cannot settle the achievements or limits of checkpoint inhibitors, chemotherapy, targeted drugs, antibody-drug conjugates or other modalities.

The supplied review retained the main text of the 2025 CAR-T article but its extraction was truncated during the references; figures were not independently inspected. Its identified prose supports the barriers, dated approval statements and reported clinical examples above, while limiting assessment of the complete reference trail and underlying studies. The Norwegian registry article was available in a complete retained extraction. These access conditions support a bounded account of the supplied evidence, not a comprehensive assessment of all contemporary treatments.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration, not an established consensus standard: randomized trials in at least three common metastatic carcinomas should show that a single defined platform produces durable complete remission in a majority of enrolled patients within each carcinoma, with acceptable toxicity. Assessing the majority separately within each carcinoma would prevent a strong result in one population from concealing failure in another.
completion_criteria.label: Majority durable complete remission within each of at least three carcinomas

completion_criteria.text: Proposed protocol requirements: define the platform and permitted disease-specific adaptations, eligible populations, comparator, remission assessments, duration of remission, treatment cessation, subsequent anticancer treatment and survival endpoints in advance. Follow-up should extend for several years after treatment stops and examine whether survival plateaus alongside sustained remission. Months of additional median progression-free survival alone would not meet the proposed bar.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified endpoints assess remission and survival years after treatment stops

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and safety requirements: confirm outcomes across independent centers and reproducible manufacturing and delivery conditions, with transparent accounting for enrollment, treatment failures, deaths, loss to follow-up and later treatments. Prespecified safety boundaries should address treatment-related mortality, severe organ injury, persistent disability and long-term toxicity. Practical evaluation should establish which patients can receive the platform and what specialized infrastructure it requires.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproduce outcomes with transparent accounting and safety boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Interpretive boundary: sustained complete remission, survival plateaus and complementary evidence of low residual disease would strengthen the case for a potentially curative capability. A plateau alone would not prove elimination of every dormant malignant cell. Finite trials would establish the breadth and durability demonstrated in their enrolled populations and follow-up period; additional carcinomas, patient groups and longer-term recurrence risks would remain separate questions.
completion_criteria.label: Curative interpretations acknowledge finite follow-up and unproven dormant-cell elimination

related_concepts.text: CLM-13, Population screening that shifts unscreened lethal cancers to a curable stage, addresses an earlier point in the disease course. The supplied roster confirms this designation. Screening aims to find disease while curative treatment remains possible; CLM-07 aims to eradicate carcinoma that has already metastasized. Better screening could reduce the number of people needing this capability, but a screening test alone does not eliminate established metastases.

CLM-01, Programmable antigen-specific immune tolerance, overlaps in the need to distinguish intended targets from healthy tissues. Its goal is selective immune restraint, whereas an immune-based implementation of CLM-07 would need effective antitumor activity with controlled normal-tissue injury. The documented problem of shared tumor and normal-tissue antigens makes selective immune control relevant without making the two capabilities equivalent.

Conceptual comparison with CLM-02, Clearance of persistent viral reservoirs that force lifelong therapy: both concern durable freedom from disease despite persistent, potentially hidden populations. The biological targets and mechanisms differ—infected reservoir cells versus malignant clones—and a method that clears one would not establish clearance of the other. The comparison highlights the distinction between long-term suppression and elimination without supplying evidence for a shared solution.

Conceptual comparison with CLM-09, Curative in vivo genome writing beyond the liver: genome writing could conceivably contribute to a future treatment platform, but its defining advance is delivery and correction of genetic information in relevant tissues. CLM-07 is defined by a clinical outcome across metastatic carcinomas and could be achieved without in vivo genome writing. Conversely, successful genome writing would not by itself demonstrate cancer eradication.

Conceptual comparison with CLM-10, Vaccines that elicit broad protection against hypervariable viruses: both raise questions about recognition breadth and escape from immune targeting. Viral variation and tumor antigen heterogeneity nevertheless involve different targets and clinical settings. Broad antiviral protection would not establish the ability to clear established heterogeneous metastatic carcinoma.

change_log.change: Preserved CLM-07 and its title while defining the innovation as a proposed, modality-independent clinical capability.
change_log.reason: The concept concerns reproducible metastatic-carcinoma eradication; CAR-T evidence supplies important barriers but does not restrict the concept to CAR-T.

change_log.change: Separated documented antigen, stromal, immune-suppression and safety barriers from the proposed requirement to clear dormant residual cells.
change_log.reason: The review supports the former but does not specifically establish dormant-cell resistance or clearance.

change_log.change: Expanded the CD19 comparison to explain manageable B-cell depletion versus injury to essential normal tissues.
change_log.reason: This preserves the review’s useful biological distinction and replaces an overly simple explanation of why hematologic success is difficult to transfer.

change_log.change: Qualified the Norwegian 66.7% statistic with its 2015 population, contributing-cause interpretation and underreporting limitations.
change_log.reason: The registry does not determine a precise universal fraction of deaths caused by metastases.

change_log.change: Dated the CAR-T approval count to October 2025 and retained the lack of verified freshness through 1 November 2026.
change_log.reason: A dated review and an empty freshness search record cannot establish later regulatory status.

change_log.change: Restored the satri-cel trial population and preserved the 1.77-to-3.25-month progression-free survival result with its review-level evidence limits.
change_log.reason: The result concerns previously treated advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer, and the primary trial was not separately supplied.

change_log.change: Included the reported complete response lasting more than 30 months in diffuse midline glioma while marking its scope distinction.
change_log.reason: Individual durable responses prevent a blanket dismissal of solid-tumor results, but glioma is outside carcinoma and does not demonstrate broad reproducibility.

change_log.change: Qualified checkpoint-inhibitor cure assertions and the historical leukemia and germ-cell analogy.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish the asserted cure outcomes or treatment history; the analogy remains explicitly illustrative.

change_log.change: Refined completion criteria with a majority within each carcinoma, acceptable toxicity, predefined endpoints, independent reproducibility and practical delivery boundaries.
change_log.reason: These make the proposed demonstration assessable without presenting chosen thresholds as published standards or equating survival plateaus with microscopic eradication.

change_log.change: Confirmed the CLM-13 mapping from the supplied roster and added bounded comparisons with other relevant concepts.
change_log.reason: The roster resolves the review’s designation uncertainty; conceptual overlaps do not justify merging distinct entries.

change_log.change: Preserved extraction and source-access limitations in the evidence account.
change_log.reason: The CAR-T extraction ends during the references, figures were not independently inspected, and underlying trial evidence was not separately supplied.

unresolved_issues: Regulatory status and the broader treatment landscape after the October 2025 review remain unverified; no freshness search record was supplied.
The supplied evidence does not establish checkpoint-inhibitor cure rates in the named populations or comparative cure outcomes across existing treatment modalities.
Dormant-cell clearance remains a proposed requirement without a demonstrated mechanism or validated proof of complete elimination in the supplied evidence.
The primary satri-cel trial and the underlying evidence for the reported glioma response were not separately supplied, limiting independent assessment of endpoints, follow-up and generalizability.
The exact remission duration, acceptable toxicity thresholds, platform boundaries and eligible populations for the proposed completion trials remain to be specified.
Several years of remission and a survival plateau would leave uncertainty about later recurrence and microscopic residual disease.
The historical leukemia and germ-cell treatment comparison remains unverified by the supplied sources and is retained only as an explicitly limited analogy.

brief.title: Lasting freedom from cancer that has spread
possible: People whose cancer has spread to distant parts of the body could finish treatment and remain free of detectable cancer for years. The goal is a treatment that achieves this in most patients across several common carcinomas, cancers of surface and lining tissues, while preserving essential healthy tissue.
The treatment would also need to eliminate hidden cancer cells that could later restart the disease. It could use drugs, immune treatments, engineered cells or combinations.
why: Cancer that has spread contributes substantially to deaths from solid tumors. Lasting remission, meaning no detectable cancer, could reduce deaths and give patients more years without active treatment, fewer repeated treatment courses and less cumulative treatment burden.

sources.who: Hanna Dillekås, Michael S Rogers and Oddbjørn Straume
sources.showed: Their Norwegian registry study found that cancer spread was recorded as a contributing cause in about two-thirds of solid-tumor deaths. The proportion varied substantially by tumor type.
sources.quote: For solid tumors, 66.7% of cancer deaths were registered with metastases as a contributing cause.
sources.cited_for: Cancer spread contributes substantially to the burden of fatal solid cancer.
sources.not_established: Underreporting prevented an exact estimate of deaths caused by cancer spread, and the findings do not establish a worldwide proportion.

sources.showed: Their review described progress and barriers in CAR-T therapy, which engineers immune cells to recognize cancer. It reported longer survival without cancer worsening in a stomach cancer trial and tumor regression in brain cancers.
sources.quote: dual-target strategies have induced tumor regression in most glioblastoma patients
sources.cited_for: Engineered immune cells can act against solid tumors, but recognition, access and healthy-tissue injury remain barriers.
sources.not_established: The reported results do not establish lasting, treatment-free remission in most patients across several common metastatic carcinomas.

shown: A review by Manh-Cuong Vo and colleagues reported that satri-cel, an engineered immune-cell treatment, delayed cancer worsening in a randomized trial of previously treated advanced stomach or stomach–oesophagus junction cancer. This establishes clinical activity, but does not establish lasting freedom from cancer.

The review also described an individual complete response lasting more than 30 months in a brain cancer. That result shows that prolonged responses can occur, but the disease was outside the carcinoma target and an individual response cannot establish reliable success.
missing: A treatment has yet to produce lasting, treatment-free complete remission in most patients across several common metastatic carcinomas.
Treatment must reach diverse cancer cells, including those that lose the feature it targets, while sparing essential healthy tissue.
Hidden, inactive cancer cells must be eliminated or prevented from restarting disease.
Independent centers must reproduce the results with consistent delivery and acceptable long-term harm.

milestones.label: Most patients achieve lasting remission across three carcinomas
milestones.explanation: Randomized trials would have to show lasting complete remission in most patients within each carcinoma, with acceptable harm. Separate success in each would establish breadth without hiding failures.

milestones.label: Remission and survival persist years after treatment ends
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to define treatment, eligible patients, comparisons and outcomes beforehand, then follow patients for years after treatment stops. This would distinguish lasting freedom from cancer from a brief delay in worsening.

milestones.label: Independent centers reproduce results within clear safety limits
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to reproduce outcomes with consistent production and delivery, accounting for every patient and later treatment within predefined safety limits. This would establish reliability and who can receive treatment.

milestones.label: Claims of cure reflect remaining uncertainty
milestones.explanation: Sustained remission, survival that levels off and little detectable residual disease would strengthen the case for cure. Limited follow-up would still leave later recurrence and elimination of every inactive cancer cell unresolved.

uncertain: How long must remission last, and how much treatment harm is acceptable, before this capability counts as achieved?
How can tests distinguish elimination of hidden cancer cells from prolonged inactivity?
How much can treatment vary between cancer types while still counting as the same treatment platform?

page.title: Treatment-free complete remission of metastatic carcinoma
page.definition: A metastatic carcinoma arises in epithelial cells, which cover body surfaces and line organs, and has spread from its primary site to a distant part of the body. In each of several such carcinoma types, the same treatment platform causes all clinical signs and symptoms of cancer to disappear in most patients assigned to receive it. Their complete remission persists after all anticancer treatment ends.

goal.need: In Norway in 2015, metastases were recorded as contributing to 6,483 of 9,722 deaths from solid tumours. Metastases diagnosed later in the illness were underreported. People can live for years with metastatic cancer, often relying on continuous or repeated therapy to control its growth. If remission persisted after treatment ended, patients could spend those years without scheduling further courses or facing side effects from additional doses. Follow-up would still be needed for recurrence and lasting effects of earlier treatment.

figures.caption: Deaths with recorded metastases in Norway in 2015
figures.note: Metastases were registered as a contributing cause. These are registry associations; the solid-tumour category also includes cancers outside carcinoma.

statements.body: National Cancer Institute, Metastasis Research Network
statements.quote: discover solutions to prevent, control and ultimately eradicate it.
statements.context: “It” refers to cancer metastasis. The programme page was updated on 2 September 2026.

statements.body: National Cancer Institute, National Cancer Plan
statements.quote: Effective treatment, with minimal side effects, is accessible to all people with all cancers, including those with rare cancers, metastatic cancers, and treatment-resistant disease.

statements.body: Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer, checklist for phase III trials in immuno-oncology
statements.quote: lasting antitumor immunity in the absence of ongoing therapy
statements.context: The checklist calls for identifying immunotherapy regimens whose benefit persists after patients stop treatment.

completion.title: Independent studies reproduce five-year treatment-free remission in a majority across three carcinoma types.
completion.criterion: For each of at least three metastatic carcinoma types, two independent prospective controlled studies test the same defined platform. In each study, more than 50% of all patients of that type assigned to the platform must remain alive and in documented complete remission for at least 5 consecutive years without anticancer treatment. Count from the later of first documented complete remission and the end of all anticancer therapy. Count recurrence, further anticancer therapy, death or unavailable follow-up within the interval as failure. Use the registered protocol's RECIST criteria and disease-specific adaptations, and meet its prespecified toxicity limits.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; an operational synthesis because no external body defines the combined capability.
completion.basis: Five years in complete remission is a qualified clinical landmark. In a survey of 126 oncologists and trainees, 120 regarded five years without progression after stopping treatment as consistent with cure. ESMO-MCBS v2.0 scores curative potential using survival plateaus and a persistent survival advantage, with the landmark depending on control-arm survival. The Atlas defines the combined requirement for complete remission off all treatment, a majority in each study, three carcinoma types and independent replication. Recurrence remains possible after five years.

milestones.title: A carcinoma treatment shows antitumour activity in a relevant nonclinical model.
milestones.criterion: A candidate shows antitumour activity in a nonclinical model selected for its target and mechanism of action. The pharmacology and safety findings support initial human testing under the guidance applicable to the product.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH S9 section 2.1, for pharmaceuticals; FDA's 2013 preclinical guidance supplies the cellular- and gene-therapy counterpart.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary characterization of the mechanism(s) of action and schedule dependencies as well as anti-tumor activity of the pharmaceutical should have been made.

milestones.title: A carcinoma treatment reaches a tolerated dose or schedule in a phase 1 trial.
milestones.criterion: Patients receive the candidate in an authorised phase I trial. At least one administered dose or schedule meets the protocol's prespecified tolerability rules over its toxicity assessment period.
milestones.set_by: National Cancer Institute, published description of phase 1 cancer trials; numerical toxicity boundaries are protocol-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: whether people can tolerate it, and the highest dose that people can tolerate.

milestones.title: A patient with metastatic carcinoma achieves a RECIST 1.1 complete response.
milestones.criterion: All non-nodal target and non-target lesions disappear. All pathological lymph nodes measure less than 10 mm in short axis, applicable tumour markers normalise, and no new lesion appears. In a nonrandomised trial with response as the primary endpoint, confirm the complete response on a repeat assessment at least 4 weeks later.
milestones.set_by: RECIST Working Group, revised Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: Complete Response (CR): Disappearance of all target lesions.

milestones.title: A carcinoma treatment improves overall survival in a randomized trial with acceptable toxicity.
milestones.criterion: A randomised controlled trial measures overall survival from randomisation to death from any cause in the intention-to-treat population. The experimental group meets the prespecified statistical boundary for superior overall survival, and the toxicity profile is acceptable.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics, section III.A.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstration of a statistically significant improvement in overall survival can be considered to be clinically significant if the toxicity profile is acceptable

milestones.title: A patient with metastatic carcinoma remains in complete remission for at least 5 years.
milestones.criterion: A patient with metastatic carcinoma remains in documented complete remission for at least 5 years from the first assessment showing complete remission. Follow-up establishes continued remission through that anniversary. Report the date of last anticancer treatment separately so that the portion of remission spent off therapy can be determined.
milestones.set_by: Clinical convention described by the National Cancer Institute in Cancer Prognosis; this is a qualified remission landmark, not a universal definition of cure.
milestones.threshold_quote: If you remain in complete remission for 5 years or more, some doctors may say that you are cured.

milestones.title: Most responders to a checkpoint inhibitor combination can stop treatment without relapse.
milestones.criterion: In phase I or II trials of a combination that blocks PD-1 or PD-L1, a substantial proportion of responses last more than one year, are complete or near complete, or meet both conditions. Most responders can discontinue treatment without relapse during reported follow-up. The one-year interval measures response duration. Report time off treatment separately.
milestones.set_by: Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer, phase III immuno-oncology checklist, table 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: treatment can be discontinued without relapse in most of the responders

not_found: No universal numerical toxicity limit for curative treatment across metastatic carcinomas was found.
No validated clinical test proving elimination of every dormant carcinoma cell was found.
No NCI, ESMO or SITC statement rejecting durable treatment-free remission across metastatic carcinomas as a goal was identified.
No independent controlled studies meeting the five-year treatment-free majority threshold in each of three metastatic carcinoma types were identified.

results.finding: Among 6 treated patients with metastatic breast cancer, 1 had a complete response ongoing at 66 months.
results.detail: Treatment included selected tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and a short course of pembrolizumab. The paper reports the response duration but does not specify the exact date complete response began.
results.quote: Our patient 4136 with advanced breast cancer had a complete response ongoing at 66 months in response to TIL transfer where 76% of their neoantigen-reactive T cells targeted HLA class II antigens.

results.finding: DS-8201a produced complete tumor regression in 3 of 5 mice bearing ST225 breast cancer xenografts.
results.detail: The paper does not name the guidance used. It reports that the nonclinical safety profile supported entry into human trials and that phase I dose escalation began in Japan in August 2015.
results.quote:
complete
tumor regression was observed on day 21 in 3 of 5 mice treated
with DS-8201a, not T-DM1 (Fig. 5B).

results.finding: Concurrent CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade inhibited tumor growth versus control in MC38 and CT26 mice (8–12 and 10 per group, respectively, p<0.0001 in both).
results.detail: The tumor studies used mouse surrogate antibodies. One high-dose macaque died from acute gastric dilatation, and a treatment relationship could not be ruled out.
results.quote: Synergistic antitumor activity in mouse MC38 and CT26 colorectal tumor models was observed with concurrent, but not sequential CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade.

results.finding: In RENCA mice, neither antibody showed single-agent activity and the combination showed little or no activity. Sample size and effect magnitude are unreported.
results.quote: Interrogation of other tumor models such as RENCA renal carcinoma and B16F10 melanoma demonstrated no single agent activity and little or no combinatorial activity.

results.finding: AZD9291 produced complete macroscopic regression in 10 of 12 EGFR L858R/T790M H1975 xenografts.
results.detail: The paper documents initiation of first-in-human dosing and acknowledges preclinical toxicology studies, whose results it does not present.
results.quote: In H1975 xenografts, 5 mg/kg/day AZD9291 resulted in complete responses in 10 of 12 tumors.

results.finding: In 2 selected AURA phase I patients receiving AZD9291, 1 had CTCAE grade 1 diarrhea.
results.detail: The two patients were selected for objective response from the six-patient starting cohort.
results.quote: in these two cases there were no rash events and only one reported CTCAE Grade 1 diarrhea.

results.finding: Both reported patients with stage IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC had confirmed RECIST 1.1 partial responses to AZD9291.
results.quote: the two confirmed partial responses described in this paper

results.finding: Among 24 phase 1 trastuzumab deruxtecan recipients, including patients with breast carcinoma, zero dose-limiting toxicities occurred.
results.detail: The safety results are pooled across tumour types. The authors reported that the maximum tolerated dose was not reached and identified 5·4 or 6·4 mg/kg as likely phase 2 doses.
results.quote: Up to the study cutoff date of Feb 1, 2017, no dose-limiting toxic effects, substantial cardiovascular toxic effects, or deaths occurred.

results.finding: MDX-1106 phase I trial including 14 colorectal carcinoma patients: zero dose-limiting toxicities after the initial infusion across the 39-patient trial.
results.detail: The protocol assessed tolerability in mixed-tumor dose cohorts. The finding applies to the initial infusion.
results.quote: MDX-1106 was well-tolerated: no DLTs were observed after one dose, and an MTD was not defined in this study.

results.finding: MDX-1106 phase I trial including six non-small-cell lung carcinoma patients: zero dose-limiting toxicities after the initial infusion across the 39-patient trial.
results.detail: The protocol assessed tolerability in mixed-tumor dose cohorts. The finding applies to the initial infusion.
results.quote: MDX-1106 was well-tolerated: no DLTs were observed after one dose, and an MTD was not defined in this study.

results.finding: MDX-1106 phase I trial including one renal cell carcinoma patient: zero dose-limiting toxicities after the initial infusion across the 39-patient trial.
results.detail: The protocol assessed tolerability in mixed-tumor dose cohorts. The finding applies to the initial infusion.
results.quote: MDX-1106 was well-tolerated: no DLTs were observed after one dose, and an MTD was not defined in this study.

results.finding: MDX-1106 produced one RECIST 1.0 complete response among 14 patients with metastatic colorectal carcinoma.
results.quote: One durable complete response (CRC) and two partial responses (PRs; melanoma, RCC) were seen.

results.finding: Among 14 patients with metastatic colorectal carcinoma treated with MDX-1106, one had an ongoing complete response lasting 21+ months.
results.detail: The 21+ months measure response duration. Time off treatment cannot be determined from the report.
results.quote: A 67-year-old male with CRC metastatic to intra-abdominal lymph nodes received five doses of MDX-1106 and experienced a CR persisting 21+ months.

results.finding: The sole metastatic renal cell carcinoma patient treated with MDX-1106 had a partial response lasting 16+ months without further therapy.
results.detail: The paper measures 16+ months from partial response and does not separately quantify the interval from the final dose to last follow-up.
results.quote: this evolved to an overall PR after two additional doses, lasting 16+ months without further therapy

results.finding: In DESTINY-Breast03, 55 of 261 patients assigned to trastuzumab deruxtecan had a confirmed RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.detail: The published complete-response count is for the full deruxtecan arm. Individual lesion measurements and tumour marker values are unavailable in the text.
results.quote:
In the trastuzumab deruxtecan 
group, 55 (21%) patients had a complete response

results.finding: In DESTINY-Breast03 (n=524), trastuzumab deruxtecan versus trastuzumab emtansine yielded an overall survival hazard ratio of 0.64.
results.detail: Drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 15% versus 3% of treated patients. Drug-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 20% versus 7%.

results.finding: In CheckMate 8HW, 90 of 296 patients assigned nivolumab plus ipilimumab achieved a confirmed RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.quote:
Complete responses were 
reported in 90 (30%) of 296 patients in the nivolumab plus 
ipilimumab group and 80 (28%) of 286 patients in the 
nivolumab group

results.finding: Among 209 CheckMate 8HW responders to nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 43% achieved a complete response.
results.detail: The 43% is calculated from the reported complete and objective response counts. The two-year treatment cap and aggregate treatment completion counts do not establish how many responders remained relapse-free after stopping.
results.quote:
Complete responses were 
reported in 90 (30%) of 296 patients in the nivolumab plus 
ipilimumab group and 80 (28%) of 286 patients in the 
nivolumab group

results.finding: Among 703 treated CheckMate 8HW patients, 252 deaths were reported across the combination and nivolumab groups.
results.detail: The statistically significant time-to-event result was for progression-free survival. The crude death counts do not account for time to death or censoring.
results.quote:
Among the 703 patients who received at least one dose 
of treatment, 252 deaths were reported (103 [29%] of 
352 patients in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab group 
and 149 [42%] of 351 patients in the nivolumab group).

results.finding: CROWN reported 15 overall complete responses among 149 patients assigned to lorlatinib for advanced ALK-positive NSCLC.
results.detail: Table 1 gives aggregate overall and intracranial response counts without linking them at the patient level.

results.finding: In 808 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and docetaxel yielded an overall survival hazard ratio of 0.69 versus placebo.
results.detail: The end-of-study estimates include 50 patients who crossed over to pertuzumab and remained in the placebo group for the survival analysis. The earlier confirmatory analysis is cited without its statistical boundary.
results.quote: Median overall survival was 57·1 months (95% CI 50-72) in the pertuzumab group and 40·8 months (36-48) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0·69, 95% CI 0·58-0·82)

results.finding: CheckMate 8HW randomized 839 patients with metastatic colorectal carcinoma. In the centrally confirmed subset, the OS HR for nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab was 0.61.
results.detail: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab missed its prespecified OS threshold (P = 0.0432 against P < 0.006). The update reported no new safety concerns or additional treatment-related deaths.
results.quote: NIVO + IPI demonstrated significant OS benefit compared with NIVO across all lines [hazard ratio (HR) 0.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.46-0.82, P = 0.0009] and with chemotherapy in 1L (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.24-0.57, P < 0.0001).

results.finding: In metastatic NSCLC, 7 of 154 patients assigned to first-line pembrolizumab achieved a RECIST 1.1 complete response.
In KEYNOTE-024 (n = 305), the overall survival hazard ratio for first-line pembrolizumab versus platinum-based chemotherapy was 0.62.
results.detail: The second interim analysis used the prespecified alpha. The five-year analysis had no allocated alpha.
results.quote: Median OS was 26.3 months (95% CI, 18.3 to 40.4) for pembrolizumab and 13.4 months (9.4-18.3) for chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.48 to 0.81).

results.finding: In KEYNOTE-010 (n=1,033), pembrolizumab versus chemotherapy had an overall survival hazard ratio of 0.66 in locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC.
results.detail: The hazard ratio comes from the table. The source is an ESMO congress abstract and does not establish journal peer review.

results.finding: HER2-positive metastatic breast carcinoma (n=1): one complete radiological response on CT.
results.quote: Despite this, CT restaging 2 months later showed complete radiological response with no evidence of metastatic disease.

results.finding: HER2-positive metastatic breast carcinoma (n=1): progression-free for 6.5 years after treatment cessation following a complete radiological response.
results.detail: Trastuzumab was held because left ventricular ejection fraction fell to 50%. The first CT showing complete response occurred during the hold, before the decision to stop permanently.
results.quote:
On serial follow-up since ceasing treatment over 6.5 years, the patient has remained progression-free (
figures 3
and
4
).

results.finding: In 1 patient with metastatic colorectal carcinoma, complete radiological and biological response followed 12 courses of cetuximab plus irinotecan.
results.detail: The February 2005 response was followed by nodal progression in November 2006. The September 2009 response began the later durable remission.
results.quote: Complete radiological and biological response was obtained in February 2005 and the treatment was stopped at this date, after 12 courses of cetuximab and irinotecan.

results.finding: One patient with metastatic colorectal carcinoma remained in complete remission for 8 years, from September 2009 to September 2017.
results.quote:
By September 2009, the patient achieved complete response and treatment was stopped.
The last evaluation with clinical examination, CT scan and CEA dosing performed in September 2017 found no evidence of recurrence.

results.finding: Among 10 metastatic colorectal carcinoma patients in phase I dose escalation, 0 had a dose-limiting toxicity.
results.detail: Six received botensilimab plus balstilimab and four received botensilimab alone. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached.
results.quote: There were no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) in either BOT monotherapy or BOT plus BAL combination therapy dose-escalation cohorts, which was the primary endpoint of the study.

results.finding: Botensilimab plus balstilimab yielded 1 confirmed RECIST 1.1 complete response among 101 evaluable metastatic colorectal carcinoma patients.
results.detail: Figure 2 identifies the complete response as confirmed. The source reports the RECIST classification without listing the individual lesion measurements or tumour-marker values.

results.finding: With botensilimab plus balstilimab for metastatic colorectal carcinoma, 11 of 17 confirmed responders had ongoing responses at cutoff.
results.detail: Median follow-up was 10.3 months. Ongoing response at cutoff does not establish time off treatment. The paper gives no aggregate off-treatment duration or relapse-free proportion for confirmed responders who stopped.
results.quote: Eleven of the 17 responding patients had ongoing responses at the time of the data cutoff.

results.finding: Median overall survival was 20.9 months in 101 evaluable metastatic colorectal carcinoma patients receiving botensilimab plus balstilimab.
results.detail: The authors described the safety profile as manageable in this phase I cohort. Overall survival was exploratory, with a 95% CI of 10.6 months to not reached.

results.finding: Among 25 patients with advanced breast carcinoma receiving phase Ib pembrolizumab, zero discontinued because of treatment-related adverse events.
results.quote: No treatment-related discontinuations or deaths occurred.

results.finding: Among 25 patients with advanced breast carcinoma treated with pembrolizumab, zero achieved a RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.detail: The source describes the cohort as having advanced breast cancer and gives no metastatic-only denominator.
results.quote: Three patients experienced partial response (PR) and none experienced complete response (CR), resulting in an ORR of 12.0% (95% CI, 2.5%-31.2%); 16% of patients had stable disease (SD) and clinical benefit rate (CR + PR + [SD for ≥24 weeks]) was 20% (95% CI, 7-41).

results.finding: Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel yielded 0 RECIST 1.1 complete responses among 18 evaluable patients with metastatic breast cancer.
results.detail: Twenty patients enrolled. Two discontinued early and were excluded from the response analysis.
results.quote: Among the 18 evaluable patients of the whole trial population, 11 achieved a PR, yielding a final ORR of 61.1%

results.finding: One of 11 metastatic breast cancer responders to pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel had an ongoing partial response after stopping both drugs.
results.detail: The >24 months describes response duration. The prose gives no separate numerical interval off treatment for this patient.
results.quote: One patient has an ongoing PR (>24 months) after discontinuation of both agents due to an immune-related adverse event

results.finding: Among 23 patients treated with the triplet for metastatic breast cancer, 87% experienced treatment-related grade 3 toxicity.
results.detail: The starting schedule was palbociclib 125 mg daily for 3 weeks on and 1 week off, pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks, and letrozole 2.5 mg daily. Half of cohort 2 had at least one dose reduction.
results.quote: Of the 23 patients that received treatment, 20/23 (87%) had grade 3 toxicity and 7/23 (30%) had grade 4 toxicity related to treatment

results.finding: In the 16-patient first-line metastatic breast cancer cohort, 5 achieved a reported RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.quote: In cohort 2, a total of 5/16 (31%) evaluable patients achieved CR, 4/16 (25%) had PR, and 5/16 (31%) had SD by RECIST 1.1

results.finding: With the pembrolizumab triplet in metastatic breast cancer, 5 of 9 first-line responders achieved complete responses.
results.detail: Median follow-up in the first-line cohort was 24.8 months. The reported 25.2-month median progression-free survival does not measure response duration or time off treatment.
results.quote: In cohort 2, 31% achieved complete response (CR), 25% had PR, and 31% had SD by RECIST 1.1.

results.finding: Metastatic non-small-cell lung carcinoma (n=1) had 1 reported complete response after nivolumab.
results.quote: Over the next 3 years, regular monitoring with CEA, Ca15.3, and CT-PET scans indicated a complete response.

results.finding: Metastatic non-small-cell lung carcinoma (n=1) had a reported 5 years disease-free off nivolumab.
results.detail: Last anticancer treatment was nivolumab. The discussion dates discontinuation to mid-2018, while Table 1 records discontinuation and observed complete response in 2019.
results.quote: This led to a complete response, and the patient has remained disease-free since the treatment was discontinued in mid-2018, which is now five years ago.

results.finding: Among six patients treated for metastatic breast carcinoma, one achieved a RECIST 1.0 complete response.
results.detail: Objective response rate was the primary endpoint. Imaging was scheduled at six weeks after treatment and regularly thereafter.
results.quote: Objective tumor regression was noted in three patients, including one complete response (now ongoing over 5.5 years) and two partial responses (6 and 10 months).

results.finding: In a six-patient metastatic breast carcinoma cohort, one patient's complete response was ongoing at 66 months.
results.detail: The protocol scheduled pembrolizumab around cell infusion. The paper gives the number of doses received by patient 4136, with no patient-specific date for the last anticancer treatment.
results.quote: Our patient 4136 with advanced breast cancer had a complete response ongoing at 66 months in response to TIL transfer where 76% of their neoantigen-reactive T cells targeted HLA class II antigens.

results.finding: In a six-patient metastatic breast carcinoma cohort, one of three responders had a complete response lasting more than a year.
results.detail: Both partial responders underwent subsequent tumour resections. The reported 66 months describes the ongoing complete response.
results.quote: Objective tumor regression was noted in three patients, including one complete response (now ongoing over 5.5 years) and two partial responses (6 and 10 months).

results.finding: Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan inhibited HER2-positive KPL-4 breast xenograft growth by 97.4% versus vehicle in mice (n unreported).
results.detail: Cynomolgus monkeys were selected for toxicology because the conjugate bound their HER2. Repeat-dose studies identified lung and bone marrow toxicity among other findings.
results.quote:
DS-8201a significantly inhibited 
tumor growth (97.4% [p < 0.0001] for DS-8201a [Process 2]) when compared to vehicle control 
on Day 21.

results.finding: Fruquintinib inhibited growth of HT-29 colon cancer xenografts in nude BALB/c mice starting at 0.77 mg/kg (sample size unreported).
results.detail: The report records the Study May Proceed letter and the later NDA assessment. The conclusion about support for initial US testing draws on both because the excerpt does not reproduce the FDA’s rationale for the IND decision.
results.quote:
Fruquintinib inhibited tumor 
growth in a dose-dependent manner with activity being observed starting at 0.77 mg/kg.

results.finding: Sotorasib produced 39% tumor growth inhibition versus vehicle in mice bearing KRAS G12C-mutant NCI-H358 NSCLC xenografts (10 mice per group).
results.detail: The quantitative result is from FDA Table 6. The nonclinical safety review identified renal tubular injury in rats and liver effects in both rats and dogs.

results.finding: Belzutifan reduced tumor volume by 89% versus vehicle in mice bearing patient-derived clear cell RCC xenografts (sample size unreported).
results.detail: FDA judged the nonclinical package adequate to support marketing approval and required postmarketing carcinogenicity studies to address chronic use.
results.quote:
Similarly, in a patient-derived xenograft mouse model of human clear 
cell RCC (CTG-0824), PT2977 (3 mg/kg, twice daily for 28 days) decreased tumor volume by 89% 
compared to vehicle control group (Study# PD007MK6482).

results.finding: Trastuzumab deruxtecan plus capecitabine at the recommended dose caused 0 first-cycle dose-limiting toxicities in 7 patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer.
results.detail: Trastuzumab deruxtecan was given intravenously every 3 weeks, with oral capecitabine twice daily on days 1–14 of each 21-day cycle.
results.quote:
T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg + capecitabine 750 mg/m
2
(dose level 1) was received by seven patients, and no DLTs were observed.

results.finding: Among 355 patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma assigned to lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab, 18.3% achieved a RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.detail: The response counts are reported by treatment arm. The text gives no metastatic-only response count or baseline metastatic status for individual responders.
results.quote:
Complete responses were
achieved by 65 patients (18.3%) in the lenvatinib plus
pembrolizumab group and 17 patients (4.8%) in the
sunitinib group.

results.finding: In HER2-positive advanced breast carcinoma (n=524), T-DXd improved overall survival versus T-DM1 at the prespecified interim analysis (HR 0.64).
results.detail: Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 58.0% versus 52.1%, and drug-related discontinuations in 22.6% versus 7.3%. No grade 4 or 5 interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in either arm.

results.finding: First-line encorafenib, cetuximab and mFOLFOX6 improved overall survival versus standard care in BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (n=479, HR 0.49).
results.detail: Grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 81.5% versus 66.8%, and adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of any study drug in 26.7% versus 17.5%. Fatal adverse events occurred in 4.3% versus 4.4%, with the only treatment-related fatal event in the standard-care arm.
results.quote: Interim analysis of overall survival demonstrated significant improvement vs. SOC: HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.375, 0.632; two-sided P<0.0001); median overall survival 30.3 vs. 15.1 months.

results.finding: In advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (n = 651), nivolumab plus cabozantinib versus sunitinib yielded a hazard ratio for death of 0.60.
results.detail: Among combination-treated patients, 5.6% discontinued both drugs owing to adverse events. Quality of life was maintained, and investigators attributed one death to treatment with the combination and two to sunitinib.
results.quote:
The probability of overall survival at 12 months 
was 85.7% (95% CI, 81.3 to 89.1) with nivolumab plus cabozantinib and 75.6% 
(95% CI, 70.5 to 80.0) with sunitinib (hazard ratio for death, 0.60; 98.89% CI, 0.40 
to 0.89; P = 0.001).

results.finding: One patient with metastatic rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma remained in documented complete remission for approximately 12 years.
results.detail: The report gives the month and year of the last chemotherapy dose and the interval to the first complete-response CT. Exact calendar days for those two events are unspecified.
results.quote: She has been in complete remission since 2001, off all treatment, with no evidence of tumor recurrence as of 6 September 2013.

results.finding: One patient with metastatic non-small-cell lung carcinoma had approximately 9 years of reported tumor-free survival.
results.detail: The final anticancer treatment described was whole-brain radiotherapy. The later reoperation removed tissue that proved to contain radiation necrosis and no viable tumor.
results.quote:
9 years tumor free survival after resection, intraoperative radiotherapy
(IORT) and whole brain radiotherapy of a solitary brain metastasis of
non-small cell lung cancer

results.finding: Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (7-patient series): Patient 7 remained disease free 5 years after pancreatic resection.
results.quote:
She remains disease free 5 years 
after her pancreatic resection.

results.finding: In phase II NIPICOL, 47.5% of objective responders (n=40) with MSI/dMMR metastatic colorectal carcinoma had a complete response.
results.detail: The one-year cap measures planned treatment duration. The six progressions after month 12 are reported from trial start, without a denominator of responders who stopped treatment or a post-discontinuation follow-up interval.
results.quote: Concerning the best response rate, 19 (35.2%) patients had complete responses, 21 (38.9%) had partial responses, 9 (16.7%) had stable diseases, and 2 (3.7%) had progressions according to iRECIST criteria.

definition = "A metastatic carcinoma arises in epithelial cells, which cover body surfaces and line organs, and has spread from its primary site to a distant part of the body. In each of several such carcinoma types, the same treatment platform causes all clinical signs and symptoms of cancer to disappear in most patients assigned to receive it. Their complete remission persists after all anticancer treatment ends.". Reason: The definition's pooled-sounding phrase “most enrolled patients” obscures both the treatment-arm denominator and the requirement to succeed within each carcinoma type.

goal.need = "In Norway in 2015, metastases were recorded as contributing to 6,483 of 9,722 deaths from solid tumours. Metastases diagnosed later in the illness were underreported. People can live for years with metastatic cancer, often relying on continuous or repeated therapy to control its growth. If remission persisted after treatment ended, patients could spend those years without scheduling further courses or facing side effects from additional doses. Follow-up would still be needed for recurrence and lasting effects of earlier treatment.". Reason: The discussion of CAR-T development leaves out the burden of repeated treatment and the benefit patients would gain from remaining well off therapy.

add statement by Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer, checklist for phase III trials in immuno-oncology, 2022: "lasting antitumor immunity in the absence of ongoing therapy". Reason: The society's checklist explicitly identifies lasting benefit after treatment stops as a goal of immunotherapy development.

edit completion: criterion = "For each of at least three metastatic carcinoma types, two independent prospective controlled studies test the same defined platform. In each study, more than 50% of all patients of that type assigned to the platform must remain alive and in documented complete remission for at least 5 consecutive years without anticancer treatment. Count from the later of first documented complete remission and the end of all anticancer therapy. Count recurrence, further anticancer therapy, death or unavailable follow-up within the interval as failure. Use the registered protocol's RECIST criteria and disease-specific adaptations, and meet its prespecified toxicity limits."; basis = "Five years in complete remission is a qualified clinical landmark. In a survey of 126 oncologists and trainees, 120 regarded five years without progression after stopping treatment as consistent with cure. ESMO-MCBS v2.0 scores curative potential using survival plateaus and a persistent survival advantage, with the landmark depending on control-arm survival. The Atlas defines the combined requirement for complete remission off all treatment, a majority in each study, three carcinoma types and independent replication. Recurrence remains possible after five years."; refs = [3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 39, 40]. Reason: The criterion needs an explicit metastatic population, a denominator for each independent study and a common starting rule when remission and treatment cessation occur on different dates.

add case "Renal cell carcinoma". Reason: Seven phase II trials with long-term follow-up document complete responses in metastatic renal cell carcinoma, providing a distinct case in which to assess durability.

edit m1: criterion = "A candidate shows antitumour activity in a nonclinical model selected for its target and mechanism of action. The pharmacology and safety findings support initial human testing under the guidance applicable to the product."; refs = [9, 10]. Reason: The mouse experiment's result and dosing schedule obscure the general model-selection and safety test.

edit m2: criterion = "Patients receive the candidate in an authorised phase I trial. At least one administered dose or schedule meets the protocol's prespecified tolerability rules over its toxicity assessment period."; refs = [12]. Reason: The dose range and outcomes of one antibody trial are evidence about tolerability and do not define the phase I test.

edit m3: criterion = "All non-nodal target and non-target lesions disappear. All pathological lymph nodes measure less than 10 mm in short axis, applicable tumour markers normalise, and no new lesion appears. In a nonrandomised trial with response as the primary endpoint, confirm the complete response on a repeat assessment at least 4 weeks later."; refs = [7]. Reason: The RECIST test should distinguish a lymph node that returns to normal size from a lesion that must disappear and should omit the KEYNOTE-177 results.

add milestone after m3: "Most responders to a checkpoint inhibitor combination can stop treatment without relapse.". Reason: The sequence lacks a cohort-level test of whether responses persist after treatment stops before an immunotherapy combination advances to phase III.

edit m4: criterion = "A randomised controlled trial measures overall survival from randomisation to death from any cause in the intention-to-treat population. The experimental group meets the prespecified statistical boundary for superior overall survival, and the toxicity profile is acceptable."; refs = [8]. Reason: The lung and colorectal trial outcomes obscure the FDA endpoint's time origin, event and analysis population.

edit m5: criterion = "A patient with metastatic carcinoma remains in documented complete remission for at least 5 years from the first assessment showing complete remission. Follow-up establishes continued remission through that anniversary. Report the date of last anticancer treatment separately so that the portion of remission spent off therapy can be determined."; refs = [6, 7, 28].
